passages.text: In those days the crowd once again became very large, and they had nothing to eat. Jesus called the disciples to Him and said, “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a very large crowd.
This happened in those days.
The people had nothing to eat.
Jesus called His disciples to Him.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “I have compassion for this crowd.
They have already been with Me for three days.
They do not have anything to eat.”
passages.original: Ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις πάλιν πολλοῦ ὄχλου ὄντος καὶ μὴ ἐχόντων τί φάγωσιν προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς λέγει αὐτοῖς Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν

passages.text: If I send them home hungry, they will faint along the way. For some of them have come a great distance.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said, “If I send these people home without food, they will collapse on the way.\r\nSome of them have traveled a long distance.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἀπολύσω αὐτοὺς νήστεις εἰς οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκλυθήσονται ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ καί τινες αὐτῶν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἥκασιν

passages.text: His disciples replied, “Where in this desolate place could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus had many disciples.
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They saw a large crowd.
They saw that the place was desolate.
They saw that the people needed food.
The disciples asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Where can anyone find enough bread here?”
They said, “This place is desolate.”
They said, “How can anyone feed all these people with bread in this place?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι Πόθεν τούτους δυνήσεταί τις ὧδε χορτάσαι ἄρτων ἐπ’ ἐρημίας

passages.text: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
He said, “How many loaves do you have?”
The disciples answered Him.
They said, “Seven.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτούς Πόσους ἔχετε ἄρτους Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἑπτά

passages.text: And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground. Then He took the seven loaves, gave thanks and broke them, and gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And they distributed them to the crowd.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a large crowd in a desolate place.
He spoke to the crowd.
He told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
Jesus took seven loaves of bread.
He gave thanks for the bread.
He broke the bread into pieces.
Jesus gave the pieces to His disciples.
He told His disciples to set the bread before the people.
The disciples gave the bread to the crowd.
passages.original: Καὶ παραγγέλλει τῷ ὄχλῳ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν καὶ παρέθηκαν τῷ ὄχλῳ

passages.text: They also had a few small fish, and Jesus blessed them and ordered that these be set before them as well.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples and a large crowd.
The disciples had a few small fish.
Jesus took the small fish.
Jesus blessed the fish.
Jesus told His disciples to set the fish before the people.
passages.original: καὶ εἶχον ἰχθύδια ὀλίγα καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτὰ εἶπεν καὶ ταῦτα παρατιθέναι

passages.text: The people ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
passages.sermon:
Jesus fed a large crowd of people.
The people ate the food.
The people became satisfied.
The disciples collected the leftover pieces of bread.
The disciples filled seven baskets with the leftover pieces.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν καὶ ἦραν περισσεύματα κλασμάτων ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας

passages.text: And about four thousand men were present. As soon as Jesus had dismissed the crowd, He got into the boat with His disciples and went to the district of Dalmanutha.
passages.sermon:
About four thousand men were present.
Jesus dismissed the crowd.
Jesus got into the boat with His disciples immediately.
Jesus went to the district of Dalmanutha.
passages.original: ἦσαν δὲ ὡς τετρακισχίλιοι καὶ ἀπέλυσεν αὐτούς Καὶ εὐθὺς ἐμβὰς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Δαλμανουθά

passages.text: Then the Pharisees came and began to argue with Jesus, testing Him by demanding from Him a sign from heaven.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees came to Jesus.
They began to argue with Him.
They demanded a sign from heaven from Him.
They tested Jesus by asking for this sign.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν αὐτῷ ζητοῦντες παρ’ αὐτοῦ σημεῖον ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πειράζοντες αὐτόν

passages.text: Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit and said, “Why does this generation demand a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was present with the Pharisees and His disciples.
Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit.
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, “Why does this generation demand a sign?”
He said, “Truly, I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναστενάξας τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ λέγει Τί ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ζητεῖ σημεῖον ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν εἰ δοθήσεται τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ σημεῖον

passages.text: And He left them, got back into the boat, and crossed to the other side.
passages.sermon: Jesus left the Pharisees.\r\nHe got back into the boat.\r\nHe went across to the other side.
passages.original: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς πάλιν ἐμβὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πέραν

passages.text: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, except for one loaf they had with them in the boat.
passages.sermon:
The disciples were with Jesus.
They forgot to bring bread.
They had only one loaf of bread with them in the boat.
They did not have any other bread.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπελάθοντο λαβεῖν ἄρτους καὶ εἰ μὴ ἕνα ἄρτον οὐκ εἶχον μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ

passages.text: “Watch out!” He cautioned them. “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them.
He said, “Watch out.”
He told them, “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees.”
He also said, “Beware of the leaven of Herod.”
passages.original: καὶ διεστέλλετο αὐτοῖς λέγων Ὁρᾶτε βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῆς ζύμης Ἡρῴδου

passages.text: So they began to discuss with one another the fact that they had no bread.
passages.sermon:
The disciples sat together in the boat.
They realized they had only one loaf of bread.
They did not have enough bread for everyone.
They talked to each other about this problem.
They discussed that they had no bread.
passages.original: καὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἀλλήλους ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχουσιν

passages.text: Aware of their conversation, Jesus asked them, “Why are you debating about having no bread? Do you still not see or understand? Do you have such hard hearts?
passages.sermon:
Jesus knew what they were saying.
He spoke to them.
He asked, “Why are you talking about not having bread?”
He said, “Do you still not see?”
He said, “Do you still not understand?”
He asked, “Is your heart hard?”
passages.original: Καὶ γνοὺς λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί διαλογίζεσθε ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχετε οὔπω νοεῖτε οὐδὲ συνίετε πεπωρωμένην ἔχετε τὴν καρδίαν ὑμῶν

passages.text: ‘Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear?’ And do you not remember?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “You have eyes.
But you do not see.
You have ears.
But you do not hear.
You do not remember.”
passages.original: Ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες οὐ βλέπετε καὶ ὦτα ἔχοντες οὐκ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐ μνημονεύετε

passages.text: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” “Twelve,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus reminded them about a past miracle.
He said, "I broke five loaves of bread."
He gave the bread to five thousand people.
He asked, "How many baskets of leftover pieces did you collect?"
The disciples answered, "Twelve."
passages.original: ὅτε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους ἔκλασα εἰς τοὺς πεντακισχιλίους πόσους κοφίνους κλασμάτων πλήρεις ἤρατε Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Δώδεκα

passages.text: “And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” “Seven,” they said.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He reminded them of a miracle.
He said, “I broke seven loaves of bread for four thousand people.”
He asked, “How many baskets full of broken pieces did you collect?”
The disciples answered Him.
They said, “Seven.”
passages.original: Ὅτε καὶ τοὺς ἑπτὰ εἰς τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους πόσων σπυρίδων πληρώματα κλασμάτων ἤρατε Καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ἑπτά

passages.text: Then He asked them, “Do you still not understand?”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe asked them a question.\r\nHe said, "Do you still not understand?"
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Οὔπω συνίετε

passages.text: When they arrived at Bethsaida, some people brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His disciples arrived at Bethsaida.
Some people came to Jesus.
They brought a blind man to Him.
They begged Jesus to touch the blind man.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Βηθσαϊδάν Καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ τυφλὸν καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψηται

passages.text: So He took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village. Then He spit on the man’s eyes and placed His hands on him. “Can you see anything?” He asked.
passages.sermon:
Jesus met a blind man at Bethsaida.
Jesus took the blind man by the hand.
Jesus led the blind man out of the village.
Jesus spit on the blind man’s eyes.
Jesus placed His hands on the blind man.
Jesus asked the blind man a question.
Jesus said, “Can you see anything?”
passages.original: καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ἐξήνεγκεν αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς κώμης καὶ πτύσας εἰς τὰ ὄμματα αὐτοῦ ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν Εἴ τι βλέπεις

passages.text: The man looked up and said, “I can see the people, but they look like trees walking around.”
passages.sermon:
The blind man looked up.
He spoke.
He said, “I see people.”
He said, “They look like trees.”
He said, “They are walking around.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναβλέψας ἔλεγεν Βλέπω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ὅτι ὡς δένδρα ὁρῶ περιπατοῦντας

passages.text: Once again Jesus placed His hands on the man’s eyes, and when he opened them his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood with the blind man.
Jesus placed His hands on the man’s eyes again.
The man opened his eyes.
His sight returned.
He saw everything clearly.
passages.original: Εἶτα πάλιν ἐπέθηκεν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ διέβλεψεν καὶ ἀπεκατέστη καὶ ἐνέβλεπεν τηλαυγῶς ἅπαντα

passages.text: Jesus sent him home and said, “Do not go back into the village.”
passages.sermon: Jesus healed a blind man.\r\nJesus sent the man to his home.\r\nJesus said, “Do not go back into the village.”
passages.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκον αὐτοῦ λέγων Μηδὲ εἰς τὴν κώμην εἰσέλθῃς

passages.text: Then Jesus and His disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way, He questioned His disciples: “Who do people say I am?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a teacher and healer.
He had disciples who followed Him.
Jesus and His disciples left their current place.
They traveled to the villages near Caesarea Philippi.
As they walked, Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
Jesus said, “Who do people say I am?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς κώμας Καισαρείας τῆς Φιλίππου καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἐπηρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων αὐτοῖς Τίνα με λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι

passages.text: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus asked His disciples a question.
He asked, “Who do people say I am?”
The disciples answered Jesus.
They said, “Some people say you are John the Baptist.”
Other people say you are Elijah.”
Still other people say you are one of the prophets.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες ὅτι Ἰωάννην τὸν Βαπτιστήν καὶ ἄλλοι Ἠλίαν ἄλλοι δὲ ὅτι εἷς τῶν προφητῶν

passages.text: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
He said, “But what about you?”
He said, “Who do you say I am?”
Peter answered Jesus.
Peter said to Jesus, “You are the Christ.”
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι Ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ Σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: And Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe warned them.\r\nHe told them not to tell anyone about Him.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and after three days rise again.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus began to teach His disciples.
He said the Son of Man must suffer many things.
The elders will reject Him.
The chief priests will reject Him.
The scribes will reject Him.
They will kill Him.
After three days, He will rise again.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς ὅτι δεῖ τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστῆναι

passages.text: He spoke this message quite frankly, and Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke this message openly.\r\nPeter took Jesus aside.\r\nPeter began to rebuke Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ παρρησίᾳ τὸν λόγον ἐλάλει καὶ προσλαβόμενος ὁ Πέτρος αὐτὸν ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ

passages.text: But Jesus, turning and looking at His disciples, rebuked Peter and said, “Get behind Me, Satan! For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the teacher and leader of the disciples.
Jesus turned and looked at His disciples.
Jesus rebuked Peter.
Jesus said to Peter, "Get behind Me, Satan."
Jesus said, "You do not have in mind the things of God."
Jesus said, "You have in mind the things of men."
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐπιστραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐπετίμησεν Πέτρῳ καὶ λέγει Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου Σατανᾶ ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: Then Jesus called the crowd to Him along with His disciples, and He told them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the people.
He called the crowd to Himself.
His disciples stood with Him.
Jesus spoke to them all.
He said, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself.
He must take up his cross.
He must follow Me.”
passages.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἐλθεῖν ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι

passages.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake and for the gospel will save it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowd and His disciples.
He said these words.
Anyone who wants to save his own life will lose it.
Anyone who loses his life for Jesus and for the gospel will save it.
passages.original: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσει τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου σώσει αὐτήν

passages.text: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowd and His disciples.
Jesus asked a question about true profit.
A man may gain the whole world.
He may lose his soul.
If a man gains everything in the world but loses his soul, he gains nothing.
passages.original: Τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖ ἄνθρωπον κερδῆσαι τὸν κόσμον ὅλον καὶ ζημιωθῆναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
passages.sermon: A man cannot give anything in exchange for his soul.\r\nNothing a man owns can pay for his soul.\r\nA soul is worth more than anything else a man has.
passages.original: τί γὰρ δοῖ ἄνθρωπος ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in His Father’s glory with the holy angels.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus said these words to people living in an adulterous and sinful generation.
If any person feels ashamed of Jesus,
If any person feels ashamed of the words of Jesus,
Jesus will also be ashamed of that person.
This will happen when Jesus comes again.
Jesus will come in the glory of His Father.
Jesus will come with the holy angels.
passages.original: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ τῇ μοιχαλίδι καὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται αὐτὸν ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ Πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἁγίων
